title: Signed adjoint Weyl operators for a normalized Chevalley basis
statement:
Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional split semisimple Lie algebra over $\mathbf Q$ [def-wf-lie-algebra, def-wf-semisimple-lie-algebra], with a split Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, reduced root system $R\subset\mathfrak h^\vee$ and Chevalley basis in the conventions of [lem-sfb-chevalley-root-normalization]. Explicitly $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak h\oplus\bigoplus_{\beta\in R}\mathbf Qe_\beta$, $[h,e_\beta]=\beta(h)e_\beta$, $[e_\beta,e_{-\beta}]=h_\beta$ with $\beta(h_\beta)=2$, and $[e_\alpha,e_\beta]=\pm(p+1)e_{\alpha+\beta}$ when $\alpha+\beta$ is a root, where $p=\max\{i\geq0:\beta-i\alpha\in R\}$; the bracket is zero when $\alpha+\beta\notin R\cup\{0\}$. Put $s_\alpha(\beta)=\beta-\beta(h_\alpha)\alpha$ and
$$q_\alpha=\exp(\operatorname{ad}e_\alpha)\exp(-\operatorname{ad}e_{-\alpha})\exp(\operatorname{ad}e_\alpha).$$
The exponentials are finite sums of nilpotent adjoint operators. For every $\alpha,\beta\in R$ there is $\epsilon_{\alpha,\beta}\in\{1,-1\}$ such that
$$q_\alpha(e_\beta)=\epsilon_{\alpha,\beta}e_{s_\alpha(\beta)},\qquad q_\alpha(h)=h-\alpha(h)h_\alpha\quad(h\in\mathfrak h).$$
The signs depend only on the fixed Chevalley basis. Empty root systems are allowed.

source.place: Section 23h, Chevalley bases and Theorem 23.71, pp.508--509. Agent-formulated root-string consequence needed in the omitted details of Theorem 23.72; Theorem 23.71 itself states bracket magnitudes, not this Weyl-operator identity.

proof.text: Fix $\alpha\in R$; if $R$ is empty there is nothing to prove. Apply [lem-sfb-split-semisimple-root-decomposition] to the given splitting Cartan subalgebra. It supplies the finite reduced crystallographic root pairing for evaluation, $R\cap\mathbf Q\alpha=\{\alpha,-\alpha\}$, and nilpotence of $E=\operatorname{ad}(e_\alpha)$ and $F=\operatorname{ad}(e_{-\alpha})$. The normalized brackets give $[e_\alpha,e_{-\alpha}]=h_\alpha$, $[h_\alpha,e_\alpha]=2e_\alpha$ and $[h_\alpha,e_{-\alpha}]=-2e_{-\alpha}$. Thus all the exponentials in the statement are finite rational operators.

source.place: Section 23h, Theorem 23.71, printed pp.508--509; agent expansion of the signed root-operator input to Theorem 23.72, pp.510--511.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-integrable-sl2-reflection-automorphism] with $L=\mathfrak g$, $\mathfrak t=\mathfrak h$, $e=e_\alpha$, $f=e_{-\alpha}$ and $h=h_\alpha$. The preceding nilpotence implies its local nilpotence hypotheses, and the weight brackets supply its remaining hypotheses. It proves $q_\alpha(h)=h-\alpha(h)h_\alpha$, $q_\alpha(e_\alpha)=-e_{-\alpha}$, $q_\alpha(e_{-\alpha})=-e_\alpha$, and that $q_\alpha$ carries the $\beta$ root line isomorphically onto the $s_\alpha(\beta)$ root line. Consequently $q_\alpha(e_\beta)=c e_{s_\alpha(\beta)}$ with a unique nonzero rational $c$. It remains to prove that $c$ is a sign.

source.place: Section 23h, Theorem 23.71, printed pp.508--509; agent expansion of the signed root-operator input to Theorem 23.72, pp.510--511.

proof.text: For $\beta\ne\pm\alpha$, the two roots are independent by reducedness. Apply [lem-sfb-root-string-integer-interval] to the evaluation root pairing from step 1. Write the string as $\beta-p\alpha,\ldots,\beta+q\alpha$. At $\beta+j\alpha$ its backward endpoint distance is $p+j$. Repeated use of the assumed bracket magnitudes therefore gives, for $0\le m\le q$, $$\frac{E^m}{m!}e_\beta=\sigma_m\binom{p+m}{m}e_{\beta+m\alpha},\qquad\sigma_m\in\{1,-1\}.$$ Indeed the successive factors have magnitudes $p+1,\ldots,p+m$, whose product divided by $m!$ is the displayed integer binomial coefficient; for $m=0$ take $\sigma_0=1$. For $m>q$ the vector is zero, since the next bracket leaves the root system and its weight is nonzero. Apply the same calculation with $-\alpha$ in place of $\alpha$ to obtain integer coefficients for $F^m e_\beta/m!$ as well. This uses only the consecutive-root assertion and the bracket formula already assumed in the item.

source.place: Section 23h, Theorem 23.71, printed pp.508--509; agent expansion of the signed root-operator input to Theorem 23.72, pp.510--511.

proof.text: Put $L_\alpha=\mathbf Z h_\alpha\oplus\bigoplus_{\gamma\in R}\mathbf Z e_\gamma\subset\mathfrak g$. The remaining generators have $E(e_\alpha)=0$, $E(e_{-\alpha})=h_\alpha$, $E^2(e_{-\alpha})/2!=-e_\alpha$, and $E(h_\alpha)=-2e_\alpha$, with higher terms zero. Similarly $F(e_{-\alpha})=0$, $F(e_\alpha)=-h_\alpha$, $F^2(e_\alpha)/2!=-e_{-\alpha}$ and $F(h_\alpha)=2e_{-\alpha}$. Together with step 3 these formulas show that $\exp(\pm E)$ and $\exp(\pm F)$ preserve $L_\alpha$. Their inverse identities $\exp(E)\exp(-E)=1$ and $\exp(F)\exp(-F)=1$ follow directly: the coefficient of the $k$th power is $\sum_{i=0}^k(-1)^i/(i!(k-i)!)$, equal to $0$ for $k>0$ and $1$ for $k=0$ by $(1-1)^k$. Hence $q_\alpha$ and its inverse both preserve $L_\alpha$. This is a calculation on the displayed generators, with no assertion that $L_\alpha$ spans the entire Cartan subalgebra.

source.place: Section 23h, Theorem 23.71, printed pp.508--509; agent expansion of the signed root-operator input to Theorem 23.72, pp.510--511.

proof.text: For any root $\gamma$, the direct root decomposition and $h_\alpha\ne0$ imply $L_\alpha\cap\mathbf Qe_\gamma=\mathbf Ze_\gamma$: comparing all components makes every coefficient other than that of $e_\gamma$ vanish. The equality $q_\alpha(e_\beta)=c e_{s_\alpha(\beta)}$ from step 2 and preservation of $L_\alpha$ force $c\in\mathbf Z$. Applying the inverse to $e_{s_\alpha(\beta)}$ gives $c^{-1}e_\beta\in L_\alpha$, hence $c^{-1}\in\mathbf Z$. Thus two integers multiply to $1$, so $c=1$ or $c=-1$. Define $\epsilon_{\alpha,\beta}=c$. Uniqueness of the scalar on the nonzero chosen root vector shows that the signs are determined by the fixed basis. The Cartan formula was proved in step 2.
